work.permit: Written authorisation of the Director (Employment and Industrial Relations)

note: Read on legislation.mt, the Laws of Malta. Majority: 18, Civil Code (Cap. 16) art. 188: majority is fixed at the completion of the eighteenth year; a major is capable of all acts of civil life. Emancipation isn't held. Work: 16. Young Persons (Employment) Regulations (S.L. 452.92, as amended to Act XXIX of 2019): a 'child' is under sixteen (or the school-leaving age the Education Act sets), and reg. 3(1) bars employing a child without written permission under the Education Act. Light work from 14 with the Director's written authorisation and work/training schemes aren't held. Performers: reg. 3(2) lets an employer apply to the Director for written authorisation to employ a child in cultural, artistic, sports or advertising activities, given in individual cases on a risk assessment and with the Director of Education's no objection; reg. 3(3)(a) lets children of at least 13 take part in such activities approved by the education minister on a written notification instead: the 13-and-over route isn't held. The regulations set no lowest age for the authorisation, so none is held. Hours and night limits aren't held. Service: none. The Malta Armed Forces Act (Cap. 220) art. 3 lets the President raise the armed force by voluntary enlistment.
